thesis: A five-colour Dragon deck that buys its own curve down and then taxes every Dragon that enters — one arrival multiplies into several, each arrival is priced in damage and cards — whose kill is PROVEN on a board and unproven as a board you can reach.

stages.label: THE FIVE-COLOUR TOLL
stages.what_it_does:
Pays for a nine-mana commander and a 25-Dragon top end out of 31 land copies (26 entries), six rocks and three land-fetching sorceries — Farseek, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim — which is this stage's 35 cards. It is the binding stage. Mean available mana is 4.219 at turn five and 4.669 at six; the land-drop hit rate has already fallen to 0.525 by turn five. 14 of 31 lands enter tapped (45%, five of them always), over the one-in-three budget mana_analysis flags. Colour is not even: green on-curve 0.810 from lands alone, white and blue 0.592, red 0.515, and black 0.217 on 8 land sources — lowest of the five, with no Swamp in the 99. Rocks and dorks lift black only to 0.524.

The measurement that reframes this stage: turning model_treasures on left mean available mana unchanged to three decimals at turns one through six and within 0.001 at every turn — re-run here with both flags off, the only moves are t7 and t10, each 0.001 DOWNWARD, since a spent Treasure is gone while the commander's cast-by-turn-six rate went 0.0% to 4.1% and never-cast fell from 9,175 to 7,170 in 10,000. A Treasure is a one-shot stockpile spent only when lands and rocks fall short: it does not raise your average mana, it buys the one expensive turn — which is the only kind of turn a nine-drop needs.

Two cards here are conditional rather than flat: Mox Jasper is blank until a Dragon is on the battlefield, and Dragon's Hoard banks a gold counter per Dragon entering, so the conversion stage feeds it. Logged game 001 is the stage's stress test — Blood Moon on turn two or three left 4 Mountain, 3 Forest, 1 Island, 1 Plains. The pilot has ruled out answering that card and asked for a holistic audit of basics, pip spread and enters-tapped tempo instead.

evidence.note: all 25 members of the map's mana city are in this stage; the 26th land, Savage Lands, files with city-1 instead
all six of its members are the deck's rocks, and all six are here
Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim say 'search your library', so the map files them beside Worldly Tutor and Enlightened Tutor; in this deck they are lands
14 of 31 copies, the class mana_analysis calls over budget

stages.label: THE PRICE CUT
stages.what_it_does:
What has to happen before the deck is doing its thing is that a Dragon becomes affordable ahead of curve, and half of that is already true on turn one. Eminence works from the command zone: other Dragon spells cost {1} less with nothing to cast, nothing to resolve and nothing an opponent can remove. The other half is four printed reducers — Urza's Incubator {2}, Dragonspeaker Shaman {2}, Herald's Horn {1}, Dragonlord's Servant {1}. An oracle scan of all 95 entries for 'less to cast' returns exactly those four plus eminence and Cavern-Hoard Dragon's self-reduction, which discounts no other spell.

Priced: a reducer drawn is 0.518 assembled, 0.419 by turn six, mean turn 3.28. At four cards it is 25.8% of opening sevens and 32.1% by turn three, against the cited yardstick that '5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41%'. It is NOT the thinnest thing here: deck-audit flags thin at size 3 or less and three components carry the flag — Dragon-restricted mana at 2, THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg at 2, and THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg at 3. The fourteen sizes run 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 7, 7, 8, 9, 9, so this group is the smallest the audit does not flag. Reducer AND ramp together, the turn-five Ur-Dragon hand, is 0.417 / 0.285 at mean turn 4.546.

Sarkhan, Fireblood and Desolation of Smaug are a separate two-card component (0.306 / 0.236) because their mana is spendable only on Dragon spells: manabase.land_colors scores restricted mana as zero sources, correct for colour maths and exactly wrong for 'can I cast a Dragon'. Desolation is also a one-sided sweeper — 3 damage to each non-Dragon creature.

The commander's body is not part of ignition in practice: mean cast turn 8.172, 4.1% by turn six, not cast by turn ten in 7,170 of 10,000 iterations.

evidence.note: five of my seven sit here — but so do four protection spells and Miirym, so a ten-card city holds three stages
Sarkhan, Fireblood and Desolation of Smaug file with the Dragons, because their loudest text is tokens and damage rather than the restricted mana they exist here to add
five cards carry it in the histogram; the fifth is Cavern-Hoard Dragon, whose reduction applies only to itself

stages.label: TREASURE, TUTORS AND THE TOP OF THE LIBRARY
stages.what_it_does:
What keeps the engine running once a Dragon has landed: Treasure, a specific Dragon on demand, and cards.

Six of the declaration's seven Treasure sources are here — Atsushi, Cavern-Hoard Dragon, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone, Rapacious Dragon and Smothering Tithe (the seventh, Smaug the Magnificent, is filed under wincon because its Treasure count is the input to its own attack trigger). The group's drawn rate is 0.732 assembled / 0.618 by turn six, mean turn 2.897, and that figure is complete. Every Treasure-derived MANA figure is a floor instead: five of the seven (Atsushi, Cavern-Hoard, Goldspan, Old Gnawbone, Smothering Tithe) are named in meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled, so only Rapacious Dragon's ETB and Smaug's upkeep actually reach the mana model. Klauth's attack mana is a third kind again — spells only, and an activated ability is not a spell.

The three Dragonstorm enchantments each return to their owner's hand when a Dragon you control enters, which makes them recurring rather than one-shot: Encroaching fetches two basics, Roiling draws two and discards one, Breaching free-casts a nonland card of mana value 8 or less. That recursion is a genuine conversion-to-fuel loop and it is printed on no payoff — it is printed on the fuel.

Finding a Dragon is three cards wide: Sarkhan's Triumph, Worldly Tutor and Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon (filed in mana). Korlessa, Scale Singer is the fourth route and the cheapest Dragon in the 99 at mana value 2 — she lets you cast Dragons off the top, compounding with the eminence discount.

evidence.note: seven of its eight members are in this stage; the eighth is Smaug the Magnificent, which I filed under wincon
four of my tutors are here and three of the city's members are the mana stage's land-ramp spells
Korlessa, Breaching Dragonstorm and Roiling Dragonstorm file with the Dragons — the map hears the Dragon-typal text, not the cantrip
seven cards, matching the declared component exactly

stages.label: ONE ARRIVAL BECOMES SEVERAL
stages.what_it_does:
The engine proper, and it has two families under one roof.

ENTRY. Miirym copies every other nontoken Dragon; Panharmonicon doubles every trigger an entering creature or artifact causes; Lathliss makes a 5/5 per nontoken Dragon; Ancient Gold Dragon rolls a d20 on combat damage; Utvara Hellkite makes a 6/6 per attacking Dragon; Dragonback Assault makes a 4/4 on landfall; Sneak Attack puts one from hand for {R}. Hellkite Courser is the only card in the 99 that puts a commander from the command zone onto the battlefield — an oracle scan of all 95 entries returns it and the commander, and stack 005 refutes Sneak Attack doing the job.

COMBAT. Atarka grants double strike to every attacking Dragon, Thrakkus doubles each Dragon's power, Radiant Destiny is a flat +1/+1 and Dragonlord Kolaghan gives the team haste, so an arrival can attack the turn it lands; Scourge of the Throne is the deck's only remaining additional combat phase, an oracle scan returning exactly one now that Aggravated Assault has left. Only the first two MULTIPLY, which is why the declared leg was cut today to those two and is now thin at 2.

Two functions here are one card wide — Courser and Scourge of the Throne — and single_point_of_failure stays null: thirteen cards keep converting without either, so the exposure is on a FUNCTION, not the stage.

One correction the evidence forces: in stack 002, the deck's deepest verified cascade — entries begetting entries, against stack 001's larger single EVENT — LATHLISS'S OWN ABILITY NEVER FIRES. Every entry after her is a token, and both nontoken clauses (hers and Miirym's) exclude tokens — which is exactly what keeps the loop finite. She contributes a 6/6 body entering, not a trigger. No arrow may be drawn out of her ability on the strength of that stack.

evidence.note: Panharmonicon doubles Miirym into two nonlegendary 6/6 Lathliss copies; the final state states Lathliss's own trigger never fires because every later entry is a token
15 Faerie Dragon tokens enter as one event and Miirym copies none of them — a token is not a nontoken Dragon
Sneak Attack puts Drakuseth in with haste for {R}; the same stack refutes it reaching the command zone and names Hellkite Courser as the card that does
twelve of thirteen sit in the map's 36-card Dragon city alongside all thirteen output cards; Miirym alone files with the discounts in city-0
Miirym's address is the insurance city, so the two halves of stack 002's verified pairing (Miirym and Panharmonicon) sit in different cities

stages.label: WHAT AN ARRIVAL IS WORTH
stages.what_it_does:
What the multiplied board produces, priced per entry rather than per turn.

DAMAGE. Dragon Tempest deals X to any target for each Dragon entering, where X is the Dragons you control; Terror of the Peaks deals that creature's power; Scourge of Valkas does Tempest's job on a 4/4 flying body and counts itself. Those three are now THE ENTRY KILL's entire damage leg, corrected today from seven: Miirym and Lathliss make tokens rather than damage and sat in BOTH of that target's legs, Temur Ascendancy draws, and Garruk's Uprising matched only on trample reminder text. The target fell from 0.481 assembled / 0.356 by turn six to 0.240 / 0.153, and the leg is thin at 3. Stack 002 prices one Lathliss cast at 64 damage in twelve separately-targeted instances — 36 from Terror, 28 from Tempest — which kills a 32-life seat and leaves a 40-life seat at 8, and its final state says outright that it cannot kill both (64 < 72). Stack 001 is the larger single event: 15 tokens enter at once, every one of the 15 triggers sees X = 17, and 255 is available at a single target; the 30-life opponent dies to the second trigger.

CARDS. Temur Ascendancy draws on each power-4-or-greater arrival, Garruk's Uprising on the first and grants trample, Return of the Wildspeaker and Rishkar's Expertise cash the biggest body in the deck for a handful.

TARGETED ACTIONS. Swords to Plowshares, Generous Gift, Chaos Warp, Glorybringer's exert, and Crux of Fate, which is asymmetric here by choice — 'destroy all non-Dragon creatures' with 25 Dragons in the 99. Wrathful Red Dragon converts damage dealt to your Dragons into damage at any non-Dragon target; the stack that verified it (004) describes a board this list can no longer make and is held back, so nothing here cites it.

evidence.note: 64 damage across twelve instances: 36 Terror + 28 Tempest, with X = 4,4,5,5,5,5 at optimal trigger ordering
X is recomputed per trigger and every one of the fifteen sees 17 Dragons; Dragon Tempest is an Enchantment and does not count itself
all thirteen output cards sit in the map's 36-card Dragon city — the map agrees with this stage and cannot separate it from conversion, which puts twelve more there
seven cards carry it, which is how the taxonomy sees a payoff whose damage happens to be aimable at creatures

stages.label: THE TURN YOU MUST NOT LOSE
stages.what_it_does:
Nine answers held out of the same open mana for the same turn. The declared component is eight — Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Counterspell, Swan Song, Dovin's Veto, Deflecting Swat — measured 0.764 assembled / 0.655 by turn six at mean turn 2.796, the best-covered part of the deck after ramp. I add Eerie Interlude, which answers a sweeper at instant speed for three mana and is in no declared component at all.

The finding worth the stage: TWO OF THE NINE ARE PROBABLY NOT FREE HERE. Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat both read 'If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost' — you control a permanent, and The Ur-Dragon is a permanent only while it is on the battlefield. The goldfish reports the commander never cast by turn ten in 7,170 of 10,000 iterations and cast by turn six in 4.1%, so for most of most games these are a {2}{W} and a {2}{R} spell rather than free ones. Two limits on that inference, both real: the goldfish counts CASTS, not control — a commander cast on turn seven and killed on turn eight is counted cast while the riders are off — and Hellkite Courser is a second route onto the battlefield that it does not model at all, so 7,170 bounds the answer in neither direction. The rules half needs no stack; the frequency half is a goldfish question and is asked as one.

Eerie Interlude's stage is also unsettled. I filed it here because dodging a wrath is what it reliably does — but if the end-step return re-triggers Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas and Miirym, it is a fourth way to fire the entry engine at instant speed and belongs in conversion.

evidence.note: all three of its members are the deck's counterspells and all three are here
four sit with the discounts because their text is about your own permanents surviving
Deflecting Swat changes a target and Eerie Interlude blinks creatures, so both file with the Dragons; the deck pays for all nine out of the same held mana
five cards; the histogram splits the rest across counterspell, protection:granted and protection:redirect, which is four names for one held-up turn

stages.label: PROVEN ON A BOARD, UNPROVEN AS A ROUTE
stages.what_it_does:
TWO OF THE THREE PASSING STACKS ELIMINATE A PLAYER. Stack 001 kills every opponent on its board — final_state has opponent 1 dead at -4 and opponent 2 dead if three of the fifteen triggers were aimed there — and stack 002 kills the 32-life seat outright (704.5a) while stating it cannot kill both — 64 against two seats needing 72. Stack 005 deals 17. The deck has proven kills.

What is unproven is REACHABILITY, and it is less demanding than the scenario reads. 001 fixes its d20 at 15 for determinism; the kill does not need 15. With N tokens, X is N+2 and there are N triggers, targets locked at stacking time, so three seats at 40 needs 3 x ceil(40/(N+2)) <= N: at N=12 that is nine triggers of twelve and it holds, at N=11 a fourth trigger per seat is needed and it fails. The threshold is a d20 of 12 or better — nine faces of twenty, 45%. The real precondition is the other half: Ancient Gold Dragon must have connected in combat first.

The kill does not live in this stage. It lives in OUTPUT — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas — now THE ENTRY KILL's whole damage leg, thin at 3, and the target reads 0.240 assembled / 0.153 by turn six at mean turn 4.983. THE COMBAT KILL, after a second correction today, reads 0.204 / 0.128 at mean turn 5.027 and is the THINNER of the two. Do not add the rates; the schema cannot express their union.

This stage holds the four cards whose own text finishes a player: Drakuseth deals 10 on the attack before blockers and 7 in the air; Smaug the Magnificent deals damage equal to your Treasures to any target; Moltensteel Dragon converts life into power, the card logged game 001 dealt damage with — 16 life for 12 under a Blood Moon lock; Hellkite Tyrant is the only alternate win in the 99, at twenty artifacts on your upkeep.

evidence.note: its final_state kills both opponents on the board; derived here, the d20 threshold for three seats at 40 is 12 or better, not the 15 the scenario fixes
the second checker-passed elimination: 64 damage in twelve instances kills the 32-life seat under 704.5a and explicitly cannot kill the 40-life seat as well
Drakuseth's attack trigger is an attack trigger, not a cast trigger, so 4+3+3 fires the turn it arrives and all 17 damage stands after the mandatory sacrifice
Drakuseth, Hellkite Tyrant and Moltensteel Dragon file with every other Dragon; nothing in the map distinguishes a finisher from a body
Smaug the Magnificent files with the Treasure sources, which is also true — its own Treasure count is what its attack trigger deals

absent_stages.why: Nothing in the 99 sacrifices creatures or permanents as an engine cost. A regex scan of all 95 entries for 'sacrifice' returns six cards and not one is an outlet: Fabled Passage and Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon sacrifice themselves, Goldspan Dragon, Rapacious Dragon and Smothering Tithe only print the Treasure token's own self-sacrifice reminder, and Sneak Attack's end-step sacrifice is the price of its own effect rather than a conversion. Treasures are of course spent, which is why the claim is about creatures and permanents as an engine cost and not about resources in general. Manufacturing a fodder stage to fill the table would misdescribe the deck.

lines.note: Fifteen Faerie Dragon tokens enter as one event, so Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times and every trigger sees X = 17 (2 pre-existing Dragons + 15 tokens). 255 available at a single target; the 30-life seat dies to the second. Miirym copies none of the tokens.

Panharmonicon doubles Miirym, so one Lathliss cast becomes two nonlegendary 6/6 copies, and the entries pay Terror 36 across six trigger instances of 6 — of which 24 is attributable to Miirym's two copies, the other 12 being the two wave-1 triggers on Lathliss's own entry, which Miirym did not cause.
Panharmonicon doubles every trigger in the cascade because each is caused by a creature entering — Tempest's six instances read 4,4,5,5,5,5 for 28. It multiplies the payoff, not just the bodies.

The deck's only checker-passed arrow that reaches a finisher. {R} puts Drakuseth in with haste; the attack trigger fires the same turn for 4+3+3 and it connects for 7, and all 17 stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice. The same stack refutes this arrow ever pointing at the commander.
CLAIM: a turn-one Sol Ring is what casts a three-mana reducer on turn two, which is the sequence the 'reducer + ramp' component prices at 0.417 assembled / 0.285 by turn six. No stack covers it.

CLAIM: Dragonspeaker's {2} stacked on eminence's {1} takes {3}{G}{U}{R} Miirym to {G}{U}{R}. Stack 002 verifies the cascade Miirym runs and pays her full printed cost in its own scenario; the discount that would have paid for her is not what it checked.

CLAIM, and it is the mechanism behind the deck's biggest measurement move: a Treasure does not raise mean available mana (4.219 at turn five with and without the model) but it covers the one nine-mana turn, and turning the model on took commander-by-turn-six from 0.0% to 4.1%. Rapacious Dragon's ETB is one of only two Treasure triggers the model can actually spend.

CLAIM, and the direction is the point: Mox Jasper activates only if you control a Dragon, so a card in the mana stage is blank until the fuel stage delivers a body. Korlessa at mana value 2 is the cheapest of the 25 Dragons in the 99 — the next are Atsushi and Smaug at 4.

CLAIM, and the timing is the whole of it. Smaug's trigger is 'Whenever Smaug attacks', so it goes on the stack in the declare-attackers step and counts your Treasures when it resolves — before the combat damage step, which is when Old Gnawbone's 'whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player' makes any. WITHIN ONE COMBAT Gnawbone cannot feed the trigger. The arrow is real across turns, topped up by Smaug's own 'at the beginning of your upkeep, create a Treasure token', and inside a second combat bought by Scourge of the Throne — which is what the second-combat question in open_questions asks. Neither card appears in any passing stack.

CLAIM, stated narrowly because the obvious version is wrong: Atarka gives each attacking Dragon double strike, which doubles Drakuseth's 7 combat damage, and does NOT fire its attack trigger twice — that trigger fires once on declare. Nothing has resolved this.

CLAIM: Thrakkus doubles the power of each Dragon you control when he attacks, and Moltensteel pumps itself for life, so the pumping happens on both sides of the doubling depending on order. This is the shape of THE COMBAT KILL (0.204 assembled / 0.128 by turn six, its multiplier leg thin at two cards) and no stack covers it.

CLAIM: Sarkhan's Triumph is one of three cards that can find a named Dragon (with Worldly Tutor and Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon), and Miirym is the Dragon the conversion stage is thinnest without. Fetching is not a rules question anyone has checked here.

CLAIM: the protection component (0.764 assembled) exists to carry the conversion permanents through one sweeper, and Miirym's own ward {2} is the only printed defence in the stage. No stack has tested a wrath against this board.

map_disagreements.component: THE MAP IS UNNAMED SINCE THE RE-BASELINE
map_disagreements.why: Every region in deck_map.json carries label: null, so the names in engine-facts are deterministic fallbacks rather than a cartographer's reading — which is why a three-card city holding Counterspell, Swan Song and Dovin's Veto is called 'Bodies II'. Read the membership, not the name; the disagreements below are about which cards sit together, which is measured, and not about what they are called.

map_disagreements.component: city-1 read as an engine part
map_disagreements.why: Thirty-six cards, 38% of the deck, and it holds members of ALL SEVEN of my stages: output 13, conversion 12, fuel 3, wincon 3, ignition 2, protection 2, mana 1. It is a coherent city — every member's text is about Dragons — and it is not a stage. Anyone reading this map as an engine diagram would conclude the deck has one enormous engine and six accessories, when what it actually has is a payoff layer and a multiplier layer that the map cannot separate because both are printed in the same words.

map_disagreements.component: Protection held for the big turn
map_disagreements.why: Nine cards across three cities, 4/3/2 — and the scatter table says the same thing about the declared eight. The map files by the ANSWER each card gives: 'counter target spell' forms its own city, 'permanents you control gain hexproof' files with the discounts, 'choose new targets' and 'exile any number of target creatures' file with the Dragons. The deck does not care which answer it is. All nine come out of the same held mana on the same turn for the same reason, and that is a property of the turn, printed on none of them.

Five of seven sit in a ten-card city that also holds four protection spells and Miirym — three stages in ten cards, and the reason is that the map hears 'a condition on your own stuff' in a cost reducer and in Teferi's Protection alike. The other two are worse addressed: Sarkhan, Fireblood and Desolation of Smaug file with the Dragons, because a planeswalker that makes 5/5s and a sorcery that deals 3 to each non-Dragon read as Dragon cards. The clause that puts them in this stage — mana spendable only on Dragon spells — is the quietest line on either card and is scored as zero sources by the deck-builder's own colour maths.

map_disagreements.component: A Treasure source drawn (the map is right and my stages split it)
map_disagreements.why: The declared seven are one of five coherent components in the scatter table and city-2 has eight members, seven of which are in my fourteen-card fuel stage. The disagreement runs the other way here: I split the group, filing Smaug the Magnificent under wincon because the Treasures it counts are the damage its attack trigger deals, so it is simultaneously the fuel and the thing the fuel is spent on. That is a limit of a one-card-one-stage model, not a fault in the clustering.

Nine cards, 6/3. Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim say 'search your library', so the map files them beside Worldly Tutor and Enlightened Tutor, which cost you a card and are looking for a spell. The three ramp sorceries are looking for a land and cost you nothing: functionally they are the untapped rocks in city-5. The same words do two jobs and the map can only see the words — which matters more than usual on this deck, because two of the three fetch basics and basics are what logged game 001 turned on.

open_questions.question: Stack 001 kills every opponent on its board, but its board assumes Ancient Gold Dragon has already connected in combat, and its d20 needs 12 or better rather than the 15 the scenario fixes (derived: three seats at 40 needs 3 x ceil(40/(N+2)) <= N, so N=12; nine faces of twenty). Build the reachable version of THE ENTRY KILL instead — Dragon Tempest or Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas, with a widener, and one nontoken Dragon cast — and resolve whether the cascade reaches three opponents at 40 or state the exact shortfall, as stack 002 does at 64 against 72.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The lethality is settled and the frequency is not. After today's correction the target's damage leg is three cards and thin, and the whole target is 0.240 assembled / 0.153 by turn six at mean turn 4.983 — down from 0.481 / 0.356 — so the question of what a REACHABLE board does is now the deck's central one, and both declared kills still carry UNVERIFIED in their own titles.

open_questions.question: Hellkite Courser's enters-the-battlefield trigger, one domain and three sub-questions: does it put The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone, does the haste it grants make an attack legal that turn, and does the return to the command zone at the beginning of the next end step add nothing to the commander tax under CR 903.8?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An oracle scan of all 95 entries returns Hellkite Courser as the only card that puts a commander onto the battlefield from the command zone, and the goldfish never casts the commander by turn ten in 7,170 of 10,000 iterations — so this is the only route to the deck's largest payoff that beats turn eight. Split from a five-part question spanning four rules domains: RESOLVE_SCOPE_BUDGET caps a scenario at three sub-questions because a checker verdict is atomic over the whole artifact, and correct answers have been discarded before because a fifth part failed beside them.

open_questions.question: The Ur-Dragon's attack trigger with the commander on the battlefield: does 'whenever one or more Dragons you control attack' draw exactly one card per attacking Dragon, and may the permanent it then puts onto the battlefield from hand be any permanent card rather than a Dragon?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the payoff the Courser question exists to reach, and it is a triggered-ability question rather than a zone-change one, so it is its own scenario. Nothing in the three passing stacks touches the commander at all — 005 establishes only that Sneak Attack cannot reach it.

open_questions.question: Scourge of the Throne, alone: does its 'attacks for the first time each turn' dethrone-conditioned trigger untap all attacking creatures and grant an additional combat phase, and is 'the player with the most life' re-evaluated in that second combat against life totals the first combat has already changed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Aggravated Assault's departure left exactly one additional-combat card in the 99, by an oracle scan of all 95 entries, it appears in none of the three remaining passing stacks, and THE COMBAT KILL is declared at 0.204 assembled with nothing verified underneath it.

open_questions.question: Given a second combat phase, do Utvara Hellkite's per-attacking-Dragon token trigger, Thrakkus the Butcher's power doubling and Atarka, World Render's double strike each fire again on the re-declared attackers?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Three attack triggers in one domain, split from the Scourge question so a failure in one does not take the other's verdict with it. This is the multiplier half of THE COMBAT KILL, which after today's second correction is the THINNER of the deck's two declared kills at 0.204 / 0.128, is itself thin at two cards, and is the half with no rules work behind it at all. It also settles whether lines[8]'s Old Gnawbone to Smaug arrow works inside a turn.

open_questions.question: Eerie Interlude with the entry payoffs on the battlefield: when the exiled Dragons return at the beginning of the next end step, do Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas and Lathliss each trigger again for every returning Dragon, and does Miirym copy the returning nontoken ones?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides which stage the card is in. I filed it under protection because dodging a wrath is what it reliably does; if the return is a second full cascade it belongs in conversion and the deck has a fourth instant-speed way to fire the entry engine. A stage that is wrong about the job propagates everywhere this artifact is read.

open_questions.question: What does a goldfish target measuring the commander's ARRIVAL report — Hellkite Courser drawn, and Courser drawn with six mana available — separately from the nine-mana cast already reported at mean turn 8.172 and 4.1% by turn six?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The commander's attack trigger is the single largest payoff in the deck and nothing measures the only route to it that is faster than turn eight. A primary payoff with no target is the documented defect that left this exact deck unmeasured before.

open_questions.question: Price the mana audit the pilot asked for after logged game 001, in the terms the goldfish can answer: with 9 basics against three basic/Forest-fetching sorceries and 14 of 31 lands entering tapped, what do mean available mana at turn five (4.219), the reducer-plus-ramp component (0.417 assembled / 0.285 by turn six) and commander-by-turn-six (4.1%) become if tapped lands are traded for untapped sources at constant land count? Scope caveat to state in the answer: the model reads land and ramp COUNTS, not enters-tapped status and not colour, so it can price one third of the pilot's question and must say so.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot's own verdict is 'the bottleneck is mana consistency, not card selection', and this model agrees that mana is the binding stage — but agreement is not a measurement, and the deck's own history has a case where lowering a curve moved turn-five mana by 0.02 while trading spells for lands moved it by 0.27.

open_questions.question: For strong Ur-Dragon lists, which is treated as the primary kill — the per-entry damage cascade (Dragon Tempest and Terror of the Peaks under Miirym and Panharmonicon) or a combat multiplier turn (Atarka, Thrakkus, an extra combat)? And where do those lists put their redundancy: more entry payoffs, or more combat effects and more ways to repeat a combat?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The declaration now prices the cascade at 0.240 assembled and the combat turn at 0.204 — no reversal, and only 3.6 points apart, with both legs of both kills thin or nearly so; my stages say the cascade is the half that has ever been verified and the combat half has never had a stack. Those are two different decks wearing the same 99, and which one the pilot is playing changes what they mulligan for.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Protection held for the big turn
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Eerie Interlude, taking the component from eight cards to nine.

Eerie Interlude exiles any number of your creatures at instant speed for {2}{W} and returns them at the next end step, which answers a sweeper as completely as Heroic Intervention does and is in no component at all today. A group's size is its redundancy claim, and this one understates the deck's coverage by a card.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE ENTRY KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack), the widener half
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Either drop Sarkhan, Fireblood from the five-card widener group, or record beside the group that his Dragon-making mode is the −7 ultimate and therefore arrives three turns after he does.

Sarkhan enters at four loyalty and the mode that makes four 5/5 Dragons costs seven, so it is live on the fourth turn of his life at the earliest — and the +1 the deck actually uses is the Dragon-restricted mana that puts him in the OTHER component. The goldfish counts him as DRAWN, so as declared he contributes full redundancy to a group he answers on a clock the ten-turn window barely reaches. Removing him moves 0.240 assembled and 0.153 by turn six (the figures after today's correction of the same target's damage leg), which is why this is a proposal for a human plus a re-run rather than a correction.

findings.note: I swept every number in the artifact against the artifacts on disk and found no discrepancy. Declaration: THE ENTRY KILL 0.240 / 0.153 / 4.983 and THE COMBAT KILL 0.204 / 0.128 / 5.027, both exact; leg sizes 2,2,3,4,4,5,5,6,7,7,7,8,9,9, exact; zero intra-target overlaps and validate-goldfish-targets passes. deck-audit: three components thin at 2, 2 and 3 — Dragon-restricted mana, THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg, THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg — and the reducer group size 4, thin false, odds 0.258 / 0.321, so 'the smallest the audit does not flag' is right. Goldfish: 8.172 / 4.1% / 7,170, mana 4.219 and 4.669, land drop 0.525. mana_analysis: 31 copies, 26 entries, 14 tapped (45%), 5 always, on-curve 0.810 / 0.592 / 0.592 / 0.515 / 0.217 with B on 8 land sources and 0.524 with rocks. deck_map: 36 in city-1 at 37.9% with 13/12/3/3/2/2/1. Stack figures 64 / 36+28 / 12 instances / 64<72 / 255 / X=17 all verbatim from 001 and 002. **One honest limit on what this round can prove.** The declaration did not move between round 2 and round 3 — I re-derived it and it is byte-equivalent in every figure I checked — so there was no drift for a transcription error to catch, and for the six figures I supplied verbatim in my round-2 notes (0.204 / 0.128 / 5.027, the 3.6-point gap, the corrected multiset, the d20 threshold, +5.8 and +5.9) I cannot distinguish re-derivation from careful copying. What I can say is stronger than nothing and weaker than the claim: nothing was transcribed wrongly, and the figures I never supplied — 4.983, 0.258/0.321, 0.417/0.285/4.546, 0.306/0.236, the leg sizes 5 and 6 — are all correct against disk too.

findings.claim: the d20 threshold is 12 or better, nine faces of twenty, 45% — derived from 3 x ceil(40/(N+2)) <= N, holding at N=12 and failing at N=11
findings.note: I re-derived this independently and by a different method than in round 2, brute-forcing every N from 1 to 20 in code rather than checking two values by hand, and computing the per-seat trigger requirement rather than assuming a uniform allocation (it is provably optimal — damage is per-trigger indivisible and the seats are independent, so each needs ceil(40/X) and the constraint is just the sum). The table agrees at every row. N=12: X=14, [3,3,3] = 9 triggers of 12, holds. N=11: X=13, [4,4,4] = 12 triggers of 11, fails — the exact failure mode the artifact names. Threshold 12, faces 12-20 = 9 of 20 = 45%, and monotone above it, which the artifact does not claim but which is true and makes 'or better' safe. It also corroborates my round-2 figure it had no reason to check: at N=15, [3,3,3] = 9 of 15, six spare. Two things I want to record because they are what makes this a genuine derivation rather than a restatement. First, X = N+2 is board-specific to stack 001 (Ancient Gold Dragon plus Miirym pre-existing), and the artifact keeps it inside the paragraph about that board rather than generalising it. Second, X does not decay as seats die — Dragons you control are unaffected by an opponent leaving under 800.4a — so the count holds across all nine resolutions; nothing in the artifact depends on this but it would have broken the derivation if false. Putting the threshold in open_questions[0] as well as the stage is the right call: a resolver building the reachable version needs the threshold, not the scenario's fixed roll.

findings.claim: TWO OF THE THREE PASSING STACKS ELIMINATE A PLAYER ... stack 002 kills the 32-life seat outright (704.5a) while stating it cannot kill both — 64 against two seats needing 72
findings.note: This is my round-2 finding taken further than I asked. I asked for the singular 'proven kill' to be corrected; the stage now leads with the plural claim, states both eliminations, and gives 002 its own evidence entry rather than folding it into a sentence. Checked against the stack: 002's final_state.summary reads 'Kills the 32-life opponent outright; the 40-life opponent survives at 8', opponents[0] is life 0 with the note citing 704.5a, and the checker's step-12 finding confirms the arithmetic and the 64 < 72 bound. The label change from the round-1 'NOTHING HERE IS PROVEN' to 'PROVEN ON A BOARD, UNPROVEN AS A ROUTE' is the whole three-round arc in six words, and it is accurate: the lethality is settled on two boards and the frequency is settled on none. Keeping 'The kill does not live in this stage. It lives in OUTPUT' is the honest structural admission and it survives the rewrite.

findings.claim: Only the first two MULTIPLY, which is why the declared leg was cut today to those two and is now thin at 2.
findings.note: The one place the new text does not survive enumeration. The sentence lists five cards — Atarka, Thrakkus, Radiant Destiny, Dragonlord Kolaghan, Scourge of the Throne — and says only the first two multiply. But Scourge of the Throne reads 'untap all attacking creatures. After this phase, there is an additional combat phase', which sends every attacking Dragon in again and doubles the turn's Dragon combat damage as surely as double strike doubles one combat's. The distinction the sentence rests on is real but unstated: Atarka and Thrakkus multiply damage WITHIN a combat, Scourge multiplies the number of combats. Written as a flat 'only', it excludes the third card in its own list, and the same artifact elsewhere treats that card as THE COMBAT KILL's mechanism — open_questions[3] routes it precisely because 'THE COMBAT KILL is declared at 0.204 assembled with nothing verified underneath it', and open_questions[4] calls Utvara/Thrakkus/Atarka in a second combat 'the multiplier half of THE COMBAT KILL'. So the model says Scourge drives the combat kill and does not multiply, in the same stage. It matters materially because the leg is size 2 and audit-flagged thin; a third member would change the redundancy claim and the rate. For completeness I enumerated the whole 99 for combat-damage multiplication and found one further candidate outside this stage — Boros Charm's third mode, 'target creature gains double strike until end of turn', filed under protection — which is a one-shot single-target instant and is fairly excluded from a redundancy group, but should be named if the sentence is ever rewritten as a claim about the deck rather than about these five cards. Fix in one clause: 'Only the first two multiply damage within a combat; Scourge of the Throne multiplies the combats instead, which is a different question the declared leg does not ask.' Not fatal — the excluded card is printed in the same sentence where any reader can weigh it, nothing verified rests on it, and no green line is affected — but it is the weakest sentence in the artifact and it is new.

findings.claim: only 3.6 points apart, with both legs of both kills thin or nearly so
findings.note: The editorial call is right and the trailing clause overstates it. Dropping the reversal framing is the correct judgement: 0.240 against 0.204 is a 3.6-point gap (I re-derived it: 0.240 - 0.204 = 0.036), well inside anything a 10,000-iteration goldfish should be asked to adjudicate, and 'which of these is nominally ahead' is a worse question for a research-strategy spawn than 'the deck has two kills of the same size and has verified neither'. Withdrawing a claim rather than flipping it is also the harder and better move, and it is the second time this artifact has done it. But 'both legs of both kills thin or nearly so' is false for half the legs. deck-audit flags exactly one leg of each: THE ENTRY KILL is (3, thin) and (5, not); THE COMBAT KILL is (2, thin) and (6, not). The 6-card leg is above the median leg size of 5.5 across the fourteen the artifact itself enumerates in stages[1], so it is not thin and not nearly. 'with one leg of each kill flagged thin — the entry damage leg at 3 and the combat multiplier leg at 2' says the true thing and is the sharper version of the same point.

True, and this is the operational note the next person needs. conversion is 1,792 and wincon is 1,796 — eight and four characters of headroom. Six of seven stages now run 1,684-1,796 against 1,358-1,638 at round 1. My round-2 note said 'round 3 fits without cutting; it is the round after that which will not', and that is now exactly where the artifact sits: both fields carrying the findings above are effectively unrevisable in place. This is terminal so nothing further is planned, but if either is ever reopened, the two clause-level fixes I have specified are each net-positive in length and something must come out first. The candidates are the same ones I named in round 2 and they are still there: stages[6]'s Moltensteel/Blood Moon sentence duplicates material the mana stage already carries, and stages[3]'s ENTRY paragraph restates card text that the cards list makes recoverable. The repo's own record is radagast's output stage failing four consecutive revisions at 2,554; this artifact never breached the cap and its two longest fields are the two that were edited three rounds running, which is the mechanism that produced radagast.
